title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-throughput-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Diego Morales
release_notes: Enhances Dedicated autoscaler: finer burst throughput controls, token-bucket smoothing, improved utilization reporting and new metrics for per-fleet and per-priority SLAs. Backwards-compatible config additions; rollout via canary followed by full release.
body:
Motivation: Dedicated customers have reported tail latency and degraded throughput when fleets experience short high-concurrency bursts. Current autoscaler token-bucket parameters and utilization reporting do not expose the full picture for priority routing and throughput guarantees. This PR implements tighter burst throughput controls, a smoothing token-bucket option, and richer utilization metrics for fleet-level and priority-level dashboards.

Changeset overview (high level): 1) Introduce 'burst_throughput_limit' and 'smoothing_window_ms' to autoscaler policy schema (defaults maintain previous behavior). 2) Implement a token-bucket smoother that reduces oscillation during short bursts and preserves throughput guarantees for high-priority queues. 3) Emit new Prometheus metrics: dedicated_autoscaler_burst_tokens, dedicated_autoscaler_smoothing_rate, fleet_utilization_5m, fleet_utilization_1h, priority_queue_backpressure_pct. 4) Add per-fleet and per-priority utilization reporting endpoints and update the console dashboards. 5) Add unit + integration tests and update docs.

Checklist: - [x] Spec and Linear ticket (ENG-10234) - [x] Schema migration with safe defaults - [x] Unit tests for token-bucket smoothing - [x] Integration test against local dedicated-fleet simulator - [x] Dashboard panels and docs update - [x] Canary rollout plan in PR description

Rollout: Canary on 2 small fleets (canary tag) for 48h, monitor new metrics and latency/throughput regressions. If stable, gradually roll to remaining fleets over 7 days.

Notes: Backwards-compatible: new policy fields are optional and default to previous semantics. The smoothing algorithm is opt-in. Linked SUP-7812 captures customer repro steps that motivated the change.

perf: reduce lock contention in token accounting hot path
obs: emit new metrics for fleet and priority utilization

docs: update autoscaler docs and console dashboard screenshots
chore: bump telemetry protobuf for new metrics
ci: add integration job for dedicated-fleet smoke tests
review_comments: Amrita Singh: Please add an e2e smoke step that simulates short bursts across priority queues so we can validate no regression in latency SLA.
Author (Diego Morales): Added integration smoke test and included results in CI (see commits). The e2e sim uses a parameterized burst generator to reproduce SUP-7812.
Claire Zhang: Can we make smoothing_window_ms a duration string (e.g., '200ms') in the schema for readability? Also suggest a smaller default (100ms) after local perf runs.
Author: Updated schema to accept duration strings and reduced default to 100ms after perf runs showed lower oscillation with minimal cost.
Ravi Patel: Verified new metrics on staging; priority_queue_backpressure_pct matches expected values during synthetic load. Approving pending CI green.
CI bot: Integration job failed intermittently on first run (timeout). Re-run completed successfully.
ci_checks: integration-tests/dedicated_fleet: flaky initial failure (timeout) -> re-run -> pass
performance_notes: local sim: smoothing reduced 95th latency spikes by ~28% under synthetic 30s bursts
throughput: high-priority throughput maintained within 2% of baseline while smoothing enabled
CPU: token accounting added ~1% CPU on autoscaler control plane process at peak load
